newsitem.title: POLAND: Optimus to change 159 bonds, up profit.
newsitem.headline: Optimus to change 159 bonds, up profit.

text.p: Polish computer maker Optimus received orders to convert into shares 159 out of its 300 convertible bonds and expects the move to boost January profit by 1.3 million zlotys, the Optimus financial director said.
"It (the bond conversion) should lift our January pre-tax profit by about 1.29 million zlotys," Stefan Mroczek told a news conference on Thursday.

Mroczek said the orders were made by the underwriters of the five-year $30 million bond issue at a par value of $100,000 each, with Merrill Lynch International ordering 109 bonds converted and Polish state-owned Bank Pekao SA 50.
The bonds are exchangeable into 6,947 common shares at 38.76 zlotys a share.

Mroczek said the conversion would boost last month's result because the company would save on coupons it would not have to pay and could also free up some provisions created for the servicing of the bonds in the future.
Optimus currently has 4,406,955 shares outstanding, including the 2.5 million shares for which the bonds can be exchanged having been cleared for bourse trade by the bourse's board on Wednesday.
Mroczek said he expected the firm's net profit growth this year to be no worse than in 1996, when the firm raised net profit to 16.5 million zlotys from 9.2 million in 1995.

He said that even if all the bonds were converted in the first quarter of this year the firm's earnings then should prove strong enough for its earnings-per-share, currently at 3.7 zlotys, not to fall.

He said that this year the firm would invest largely in high-margin, non-computer operations such as multi-media and telecommunication activities, and in mass production of its Microsoft-Optimus computer, but would not give details.
